authority.rule: Accepted brief clause 8.1 makes input selection semantic. Option-contract calculations require matching underlying, expiry, strike, option right and contract identity wherever those dimensions are material; contract/expiry/delta/strike matching must be exact unless the row explicitly defines interpolation/bucketing. Clause 17 requires fail-closed behaviour when a material matching prerequisite is absent.

finding: The worker correctly made join dimensions mechanically enforceable when InputSelectionPolicyVersion.join_keys advertises them, and the prior mixed-contract witness is now refused under a full option-contract join policy. However, the runtime still treats the supplied policy as authority for whether mandatory option-contract dimensions are required at all. For D087 (Each option), an adverse policy with join_keys=('subject_instrument',) omits contract_id/underlying/expiry/strike/right. With R034 projected from contract C1 and R035 projected from contract C2, both NVDA, the public M01 seam materialised D087=101 and persisted lineage from both contracts. Thus a policy can disable a material accepted selection invariant by omission.

independent_evidence.note: Review stopped at the first remaining failed Stage-1 semantic invariant after confirming the previous advertised-join repair.
independent_evidence.prior_contract_witness_status: repaired when the policy explicitly advertises the option-contract join dimensions

repair_proposition: Close the Stage-1 input-selection class at the row-authority boundary. Material join dimensions must be mandatory because the accepted row/brief requires them, not merely because a caller-supplied InputSelectionPolicyVersion happens to name them. For Stage-1 option-contract rows, an incomplete policy that omits a material exact-match dimension must fail closed (or otherwise be proven incompatible with that row) before calculation. Preserve the newly added typed M00 selection-identity seam and advertised-key enforcement where lawful. Add authority-derived proof before production repair. Do not start Stage 2.
